title: Flex Layout
summary: Tour of the main flexbox layout properties, split into item-level (order, align-self) and container-level (flex-wrap, justify-content, align-items, align-content). Practised on a rainbow demo page and finished with the Flexbox Froggy game on intermediate difficulty.

concepts.heading: Parent versus child properties
points: Always ask whether a property belongs on the container (parent) or on the flex items (children). A child-only property placed on the container is ignored.
Container properties covered: flex-wrap, justify-content, align-items, align-content. Item properties covered: order, align-self.

A cheat sheet (CSS-Tricks flexbox guide) separates parent and child properties and lists every value; the advice is to look things up as needed rather than memorise, and revisit them when a project needs them.

concepts.heading: order (item property)
points: Every flex item defaults to order: 0, so items follow HTML source order.
Giving one item a higher order (for example 1, 10 or 20) moves it after items with lower values; only the relative ranking matters, and ties fall back to source order.
Typical use: select one child (such as the green div) and set its order to push it to the end without editing the HTML. Negative values place items first.
(Extra) order changes visual order only; keyboard focus and screen readers still follow the HTML order, which can hurt accessibility.

concepts.heading: flex-wrap (container property)
points: Default is nowrap (no hyphen): all items stay on one line and are squeezed until they can no longer shrink, after which they overflow off the page.
flex-wrap: wrap lets items that do not fit move to the next line, which makes layouts respond to narrower windows.
wrap-reverse also wraps but lines stack in the opposite cross direction (new lines go above rather than below).
Set on the container; it affects how all the children behave.

concepts.heading: justify-content (container, main axis)
points: Distributes items along the main axis (horizontal for row, vertical for column, so it flips with flex-direction).
flex-start packs items at the start, flex-end at the end, center centres them. Centering this way is far simpler than older techniques.
space-between: first and last items touch the container edges with equal gaps between items.
space-around: equal space around each item, so gaps at the ends are half the size of gaps between items.
space-evenly: every gap, including the ends, is the same size.
Only has a visible effect when there is leftover room on the main axis.

concepts.heading: align-items (container, cross axis)
points: Positions items along the cross axis (vertical for row).

The container needs extra height for this to be visible; by default it is only as tall as its tallest item. The demo sets height to 70vh (vh = percentage of the viewport height, 100vh is the full window).
Values: flex-start, flex-end, center, baseline and stretch (default).
Keep flex-wrap at nowrap while experimenting, because with wrapping on, multi-line behaviour is governed by align-content.

concepts.heading: align-self (item property)
points: Overrides the container's align-items for one single item, e.g. centre all but make one item sit at the top.
Accepts the same family of values (flex-start, flex-end, center, etc.).

concepts.heading: align-content (container, wrapped lines)
points: Like align-items but for the group of lines in a multi-line flex container; it only takes effect when flex-wrap is wrap (or wrap-reverse) and items have actually wrapped onto more than one line.
With nowrap it appears to do nothing. Values such as center, flex-start, flex-end control how the wrapped lines are spaced in the container.

concepts.heading: Practice resources
points: A hosted flex-layout demo page (rainbow items with selectors for each property) for experimenting by resizing the window.

Flexbox Froggy: an interactive game where you write CSS to move a frog onto a lily pad. Task: complete all levels in Intermediate difficulty (settings menu), which hides the direction hints; switch to Beginner only if stuck.
Example from the demo level: with a row flex container, justify-content: flex-end moves the frog to the end.

Item-level properties

.red   { align-self: flex-start; } /* ignores the container's align-items */

task.name: Flexbox Froggy (intermediate mode)
task.starting_point: Online Flexbox Froggy game with a frog and lily pad per level and a CSS editor; difficulty set to Intermediate in settings.
task.goal: Finish every level by writing flexbox CSS that moves the frog onto the lily pad, using the cheat sheet and what was learned in the lesson.
steps: Open the game and choose Intermediate in settings (optionally language / colour-blind mode).
Read the level, inspect the starting display: flex rule, and decide which axis the frog has to move along.
Write container properties such as justify-content, align-items, flex-direction, flex-wrap, align-content, plus item properties such as order and align-self, as the levels demand.
Use the cheat sheet or demo page when stuck; drop to Beginner only if needed.
task.expected_result: All levels complete with the frog on the lily pad.

pitfalls: Using align-items for something that needs the container to be taller; without a set height there is no free cross-axis space.
Expecting align-content to work without flex-wrap: wrap.
Forgetting that justify-content / align-items swap meaning when flex-direction is column.
Putting order or align-self on the container.

playground.coverage: No dedicated lesson for this video. The s09-display-flex explore demo already offers selects for flex-direction, justify-content, align-items, flex-wrap and gap with an axis readout, which covers most container properties.
gaps_and_ideas: Add a new lesson 'Flex Layout' with a blurb about parent versus child properties, plus 3-5 tasks: centre the items with justify-content/align-items, spread them with space-between, make them wrap, reorder one with order, override one with align-self.
Starter code: seven coloured rainbow divs in a gold-bordered container with height: 70vh.
Extend the existing flexbox playground demo with align-content, wrap-reverse, space-around/evenly visualisations, plus per-item order and align-self inputs and a resizable container.
Add a built-in mini Flexbox Froggy style challenge set (frog on lily pad targets) with a check against computed positions.
Add a parent/child property cheat-sheet panel.
